title: Reel 3: the Celebrity Club jam and New Orleans slang
summary: The Buddy Tate Celebrity Club reunion, the concert's success, and slang like terrible meaning good.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: The third reel of Don Albert, September 18, 1972. We were talking about Buddy Tate, you were up there in New York. You were sitting in or something and you guys started dancing?

No, I was on vacation and Buddy was playing at the Celebrity Club and Nathan Larkins was upstairs and so we just all got together, reunion or sort of, and we just started jamming up there and blowing. And these cats marched just like they do down here. And that's what the write up says in the paper this morning about the concert yesterday. How they marched in the aisles. It seems that it looks like it's only my programs here that really jumped up and down like I had them yesterday.
Well, I think it was very successful.
Well, I think it was successful both ways, financial and pleasing to the public too. As God, the comments are still coming in.

Well, I was sitting with people that knew about music and some of them anyway, certainly, and they appreciated a good lead on it, a good MC, and that's part of what Buddy Tateau. Back to the words and the way they're used here in New Orleans. If you say something is terrible in Texas, what does that mean?
It means it's bad. That's not one of the words of Ron Hill. Terrible is a nationally used word.

Yeah, but I mean, people in New Orleans sometimes will say, oh, he's a terrible trumpet player. They mean he's great. Right. Oh, he's a bad trumpet player. Yeah, well, that's the slang. Yeah, do they use that in Texas? They say that same thing, don't you? Yeah, sure they do. I thought that was true.
And some guys say, man, he's crazy. It means the guy's good. It's just slang word.
Well, Lester claims to have started a lot of that stuff.
Lester Young? Yeah. Well, the man that started most of it was Lloyd. Lloyd had a lot of slang words.
